summary: Unevaluated heartbeat 'shadowing' causes truncated final choice on resume
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated truncated final paragraph on resumed SSE/WS streams after short network blips. Impact: Nimbus Health's patient-summary generation sometimes loses the last sentence, causing incomplete records sent to downstream EHR ingestion. Frequent for streams >1k tokens and when client reconnects behind corporate proxy.

Observed behavior: After an intermediate disconnect and automatic resume, final choice is missing or ends mid-sentence. Client saw resume ACKs and resumed token sequence numbers, but the last few tokens were not delivered. The server logged a resume offset advance that corresponds only to heartbeat-only frames sent by an upstream proxy.

Why this matters: Partial patient summaries can be treated as incorrect by downstream validation, creating operational risk and manual remediation work for the customer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Nimbus Health integration configured to stream long outputs (redwood-open-7b-v2) over SSE. 2) Place client behind a corporate proxy that strips or coalesces keepalive frames. 3) Start a generation >1200 tokens. 4) Simulate a short network disruption (30-120s) or NAT port rebind so client reconnects and resumes. 5) Observe that resume completes but final sentence is missing in the assembled output.
observed_behavior: Resume proceeds without explicit finalization event; server resume offset appears to have advanced (log shows only heartbeat-only events in that window). Client-side reassembled stream lacks terminal punctuation and last clause; downstream validation flags missing fields.
expected_behavior: After resume, assembled stream should include the complete final choice and finalization metadata (end_event), or server should request retransmit/repair when resume offset does not match meaningful token progress.
logs_and_traces:
Attached excerpts: server log lines (timestamps):
- 2026-03-07T17:12:21Z INFO stream_id=abc123 resume_requested offset=20480
- 2026-03-07T17:12:21Z DEBUG stream_id=abc123 observed_frames=heartbeat-only count=3 last_frame_type=heartbeat
- 2026-03-07T17:12:21Z INFO stream_id=abc123 resume_accepted new_offset=20486
- 2026-03-07T17:12:21Z WARN stream_id=abc123 incomplete_final_choice detected_missing_end_event
Network capture (customer pcap summary): repeated TCP keepalive probes coalesced into upstream chunk that server treated as progress. See attached pcap_excerpt.txt and stdout_dump.txt.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: resume offset calculation treated pure-heartbeat frames as valid token progress when aggregated by proxy. SRE reproduced by inserting a proxy that coalesces multiple 1-byte keepalives into a single TCP write; server runtime code increments resume offset per received chunk without discriminating heartbeat-only payloads.

Repro steps validated in staging: replicated behavior when a proxy inserted a synthetic 0-length/data-only heartbeat that the runtime maps to an 'event' and bumps the resume offset. Without final end_event, the client assumes server advanced beyond the terminal tokens and doesn't request retransmit.

Correlation: INT-883 flagged earlier for 'resume offset drift' in a different code path. This appears to be a variant where upstream network transforms (coalesce/strip) change perceived frame semantics.
impact_assessment: Customer-visible: intermittent (estimated 0.5-2% of long-stream requests) for Nimbus Health in us-east when behind corporate proxy. Business impact: high due to data correctness requirements; customer elevated to enterprise SLA. Internal: potential to affect other enterprise customers behind aggressive proxies.
mitigation_attempts:
- Short-term customer workaround: enable non-streaming fallback (blocking generation) for critical EHR payloads, or set smaller max_token_per_stream to avoid long-stream resume. Nimbus temporary configuration applied.
- Service-side mitigation attempt: disable automatic resume acceptance when last received frames are heartbeat-only. Tested flag rollout in staging, reduces occurrence in 1000+ replays.
resolution_notes:
Planned fix: runtime patch to ignore heartbeat-only frames when calculating resume offsets and require a meaningful token-bearing event or an explicit end_event to advance committed offset. PR created (see related_github_prs). Backport to Dedicated clusters scheduled.
Rollout plan: canary patch to serving-runtime in staging -> probe with synthetic proxy shaping -> gradual rollout to prod us-east with monitoring alerts for 'resume_accepted_with_no_token_progress'.
Follow-ups: add an SDK-level 'finalization_ack' handshake so clients can negotiate explicit end_event confirmation with server; track as product backlog item.
resolution_status: Fix in review (serving-runtime PR); customer notified of workaround and will verify after canary deploy.
